claims.text: As-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs can form a uniformly dispersed solid-solution catalyst with homogeneous elemental distribution.
Omitting post-synthesis thermal treatment ensures homogeneous elemental distribution in PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles.
Complex high-entropy solid solutions provide a distribution of adsorption energies through their elemental configurations.
Uniform PtPdRhRuIrOs produces a broad, near-continuous distribution of adsorption energies.
The adsorption-energy distribution arises from diverse local coordination environments involving the six constituent metals.
The broad adsorption-energy distribution contains sites with binding energies favorable for activating and converting ethanol and its intermediates, including adsorbed CO and acetaldehyde.
Optimized binding of ethanol-oxidation intermediates enhances ethanol-oxidation activity.
Mild thermal annealing can induce slight elemental or phase segregation in PtPdRhRuIrOs without extensive particle sintering.
Partial phase segregation decreases local-site diversity and narrows the adsorption-energy distribution.
A narrower adsorption-energy distribution is less optimal for ethanol oxidation.
Relative to the unannealed baseline, the annealed catalyst will have lower ethanol-oxidation current density and turnover frequency.
Annealing-induced loss of active-site diversity may alter ethanol-oxidation product selectivity.
The mechanism applies in either acidic or alkaline electrolyte at temperatures up to approximately 80 °C under controlled potential.
The mechanism applies to nanoscale particles for which high-entropy effects dominate.
Catalyst configuration and adsorption-energy distribution can affect the shape and activity of electrocatalytic response curves.
